I've written your reply to Sheldon below. His B30 ships with Harlo OS already on it. I couldn't find anything published about what makes that firmware return a 409 when you save. So I flagged it to JD as a technical issue with what we know so far. The team is offline, so it gets picked up tomorrow at 10am ET. The email asks Sheldon for the details JD will need and offers a quicker route through the Discord.

---

Hi Sheldon,

Glad the B30 got to you. I'm sorry the first day has been rough, so let's get it sorted.

On the OS: work on Harlo OS is paused for now. The team is working on an alternative and will share news when it's ready. There's no date yet. Your unit's current firmware is still the one we support and will help you with.

About the 409: it's a "conflict" response from the miner's web page, which means the miner refused the save. I couldn't find anything published that says what causes it on the B30's firmware, so I won't guess. The reboots may well be part of it, because a save can fail if the miner restarts or is busy at that moment. Here are some things to try and some details to send back:

First, if you notice a burning smell, a very hot plug or any crackling, unplug the miner and leave it off. If you do, tell me in your reply.

Second, plug the B30 straight into a wall outlet with the cord that came in the box. Don't use a power strip, extension cord or UPS. If you can, use an outlet whose circuit isn't shared with a heater or other big appliance. Then see whether it still reboots, and roughly how often.

Third, give it open space front and back so air can flow. Before it reboots, look at the chip temperature in the web UI and on the screen. Note any message that shows just before it restarts.

Fourth, for the pool settings, open the web UI in a new private or incognito browser window, with no other tabs open on the miner. Enter the stratum URL, worker name and password, and press save right after the miner has finished booting. If it still says 409, please send a screenshot.

When you reply, please include the firmware version shown in the web UI, how often it reboots, the temperature you saw, and any screenshots or a short video of a reboot. That gives our hardware lead everything he needs.

I've passed all of this to JD, our hardware lead. The team picks it up tomorrow at 10am ET, and the answer will come by email. If you'd like help sooner, JD and the community are very active on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf. Mention @nullhashrate there.

Hal

I've written your reply to Sheldon below. I opened his HashWatcher screenshot. It shows 28.5 TH/s with 0.00% error and the chip at 112°F. The VR (voltage regulator) is at 181°F (about 83°C), shown in red, with the fan already at 100% auto (3,458 RPM). It's drawing 453 W at 740 MHz, with all 6 chips detected. The reboots and the 409 are now fixed, so I sent JD a second flag about the VR temperature. That way he isn't chasing problems that are already solved. I couldn't find a published VR limit for the B30, so the email doesn't claim one.

---

Hi Sheldon,

Great news that it's hashing and the pool settings saved. Thanks for the screenshot too, it helps a lot.

The screenshot shows the miner healthy apart from one reading. It's at 28.5 TH/s with 0.00% error, all 6 chips are detected, the chips are at 112°F, and it's drawing 453 W at 740 MHz. That's in line with the B30's normal rating. The one to watch is the VR (voltage regulator) at 181°F, which HashWatcher shows in red. The fan is already at 100% on auto, so the cooling has nothing left to give.

I don't have a published VR temperature limit for the B30, so I won't guess whether 181 to 183°F is fine. HashWatcher's red marker comes from the app, not from the B30's own firmware. I've sent this reading to JD, our hardware lead, so he can confirm what's normal for this unit.

In the meantime, there are a few safe things you can do. First, give the B30 several inches of open space in front of the intake and behind the exhaust. Keep it out of cabinets and corners, and away from anything blowing warm air at it. A cooler room makes a direct difference too. Second, open the B30's own web page and check whether it shows the same VR temperature and any warning. Third, if you want more headroom until JD answers, set it to a lower, quieter mode in the dashboard. It will use less power and run the regulator cooler, at the cost of some hashrate. Please don't raise the frequency or voltage above the current settings for now.

If it starts rebooting again, please note whether it happens when the VR temperature is at its highest, and send a screenshot from just before the reboot. That would tell JD a lot. Also unplug it right away if you ever notice a burning smell or a very hot plug.

The team picks this up tomorrow at 10am ET, and JD's answer will come by email. If you'd like help sooner, JD and the community are very active on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf. Mention @nullhashrate there.

Hal
